source_text: Cyprianus Epicteto fratri et plebi Assuras consistenti salutem. Graviter et dolenter motus sum, fratres charissimi, quod cognoverim Fortunatianum quondam apud vos episcopum post gravem lapsum ruinae suae pro integro nunc agere velle et episcopatum sibi vindicare coepisse. Quae res contristavit me, primo propter ipsum, qui miser, vel diaboli tenebris in totum excoecatus, vel quorumdam sacrilega persuasione deceptus, cum debeat satisfacere et ad Dominum exorandum diebus ac noctibus lacrymis et orationibus et precibus incumbere, audet sibi adhuc sacerdotium quod prodidit vindicare, quasi post aras diaboli accedere ad altare Dei fas sit, aut non majorem in se iram et indignationem Domini in die judicii provocet, qui, cum fidei et virtutis dux fratribus esse non potuerit, perfidiae et audaciae et temeritatis magister existat, et qui non docuit fratres in praelio fortiter stare, doceat eos qui victi et prostrati sunt nec rogare, cum Dominus dicat: Illis fudistis libamina, et illis imposuistis sacrificia; super haec omnia ergo non indignabor? dicit Dominus. Et alio loco: Sacrificans diis eradicabitur, nisi Domino soli. Item Dominus denuo loquitur et dicit: Adoraverunt eos quos fecerunt digiti eorum, et curvatus est homo et humiliatus est vir, et non laxabo illis. In Apocalypsi quoque legimus iram Domini comminantis et dicentis: Si quis adorat bestiam et imaginem ejus, et accipit notam in fronte sua et in manu, bibet et ipse de vino irae Dei mixto in poculo irae ejus, et punietur igne et sulphure sub oculis sanctorum Angelorum et sub oculis Agni, et fumus de tormentis eorum in saecula saeculorum ascendet, nec habebunt requiem die ac nocte qui adorant bestiam et imaginem ejus.
pass_a_gloss: Cyprian, to Epictetus, brother, and to the people of Assuras, greetings. I was deeply and painfully moved, dearest brothers, because I found out that Fortunatianus, who was once a bishop among you, after a serious fall and ruin, now wants to act as if nothing happened and has begun to claim the bishopric for himself. This situation has distressed me, first of all because of him, who, wretched man, either has been completely blinded by the devil's darkness or has been deceived by the sacrilegious persuasion of certain people, and when he ought to be making amends and praying to the Lord day and night with tears, prayers, and supplications, he dares to claim for himself the priesthood that he betrayed, as if it is right to approach the altar of God after having worshiped at the devil's altar, or as if he does not provoke greater wrath and indignation from the Lord on the day of judgment, who, although he was not able to be a leader of faith and virtue for his brothers, has become a teacher of perfidy, audacity, and recklessness, and who, instead of teaching his brothers to stand firm in battle, teaches those who have been defeated and prostrated not to pray, whereas the Lord says: You have poured out libations to them and offered sacrifices to them; shall I not be angry about all these things? The Lord says. And in another place: Whoever sacrifices to idols will be uprooted, unless it is to the Lord alone. The Lord also speaks again and says: They worshiped what their fingers made, and the man was bowed down and the man was humbled, and I will not release them. We also read in the Apocalypse the Lord's wrath threatening and saying: If anyone worships the beast and its image, and receives the mark on his forehead and on his hand, he will also drink the wine of God's wrath, mixed in the cup of His wrath, and he will be punished with fire and sulfur in the presence of the holy Angels and in the presence of the Lamb, and the smoke of their torments will rise up forever and ever, and those who worship the beast and its image will not have rest day or night.

pass_b_english: Cyprian sends greetings to Epictetus, his brother, and to the people of Assuras. I am deeply and painfully moved, dearest brothers, because I have learned that Fortunatianus, who was once your bishop, now wants to act as if nothing happened after his serious fall and ruin, and has begun to claim the bishopric for himself. This situation has distressed me, first of all because of him. That wretched man has either been completely blinded by the devil's darkness or deceived by the sacrilegious persuasion of certain people. When he ought to be making amends and devoting himself day and night to praying to the Lord with tears, prayers, and supplications, he dares to claim the priesthood he betrayed, as if it were right to approach the altar of God after having worshiped at the devil's altar, or as if he does not provoke even greater wrath and indignation from the Lord on the day of judgment. Although he was not able to be a leader of faith and virtue for his brothers, he has become a teacher of perfidy, audacity, and recklessness. Instead of teaching his brothers to stand firm in battle, he teaches those who have been defeated and prostrated not to pray, even though the Lord says: "You have poured out libations to them and offered sacrifices to them; shall I not be angry about all these things?" says the Lord (Deuteronomy 32:37-38). And in another place: "Whoever sacrifices to idols will be uprooted, unless it is to the Lord alone" (Psalm 96:5). The Lord also speaks again and says: "They worshiped what their fingers made, and the man was bowed down and the man was humbled, and I will not release them" (Psalm 96:5). We also read in the Apocalypse the Lord's wrath threatening and saying: "If anyone worships the beast and its image, and receives the mark on his forehead and on his hand, he will also drink the wine of God's wrath, mixed in the cup of His wrath, and he will be punished with fire and sulfur in the presence of the holy Angels and in the presence of the Lamb, and the smoke of their torments will rise up forever and ever, and those who worship the beast and its image will not have rest day or night" (Revelation 14:9-11).
